# M1 — Foundation: config, DB, repo, frontend, shared utils

Source: https://github.com/mcowger/plexus/blob/main/docs/plexus-piai-plan/M1.md

# M1 — Foundation: config, DB, repo, frontend, shared utils

**Depends on:** nothing. **Blocks:** M2–M6.

This milestone makes the two pi-ai hint fields exist end-to-end and extracts the
shared utilities every later stage needs. **No request path changes happen
here** — after M1, a provider can be *configured* with pi-ai hints, but nothing
yet routes through pi-ai for key-auth providers. That arrives in M2.

Design references: `DESIGN.md` → "Configuration Additions", "Shared
Infrastructure to Extract", and "Known Issues and Gaps" (registry coverage,
`streamSimple` option loss, base-URL stripping).

## Goal & exit criteria

Done when **all** of the following hold:

- `pi_ai_provider` (provider-level) and `pi_ai_model_id` (provider-model-level)
  are accepted by the config schema, persisted/round-tripped through the DB,
  and editable in the frontend.
- A Drizzle migration adds the two columns to both postgres and sqlite schemas.
- `beta/pi-ai-utils.ts` exists and exports `resolveBaseUrl`,
  `buildReasoningOptions`, `buildPiAiModel`, and re-exports `buildThinkingOptions`.
- `jsonSchemaToTypeBox` is exported from `transformers/oauth/type-mappers.ts`
  (or relocated to a shared module) so beta parsers can import it.
- Startup validation warns (non-fatally) when a configured
  `(pi_ai_provider, pi_ai_model_id)` pair is not in the pi-ai registry.
- Gates pass: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, `bun run format:check`,
  `bun run lint:migrations`.

## Tasks

### T1.1 — Add config schema fields

**File:** `config.ts`.

- Add `pi_ai_provider: z.string().optional()` to `ProviderConfigSchema` (the
  object near L558–620; add it alongside other provider-level scalars such as
  `api_key` / `oauth_provider`, before the `.refine(...)` chain).
- Add `pi_ai_model_id: z.string().optional()` to `ModelProviderConfigSchema`
  (~L168–180, alongside `adapter` / `maxConcurrency`).
- Do **not** touch `ModelConfigSchema.pi_model` (config.ts:767) — it is an
  unrelated alias-level field. The design is explicit that these are separate
  concerns (`DESIGN.md` → Configuration Additions).

**Verify:** `bun run typecheck`. Add a schema-parse unit test asserting both
fields accept a string and are optional.

### T1.2 — Add DB columns (Drizzle + migration)

**Read the `db-schema-migrations` skill first.** Never hand-write SQL.

- **Schema edits:**
  - `drizzle/schema/postgres/providers.ts` and
    `drizzle/schema/sqlite/providers.ts`: add
    `piAiProvider: text('pi_ai_provider')` (nullable).
  - `drizzle/schema/postgres/provider-models.ts` and
    `drizzle/schema/sqlite/provider-models.ts`: add
    `piAiModelId: text('pi_ai_model_id')` (nullable).
  - Match the existing column-style (snake_case DB name, camelCase TS key) used
    by neighbours like `oauthProviderType` / `accessVia`.
- **Generate migration:** `bun run generate-migrations --name add_pi_ai_hint`
  (`--name` is required on `main`; random names are rejected by CI).
- **Lint:** `bun run lint:migrations`.

**Verify:** migration file is generated (do not edit it by hand), lint passes.

### T1.3 — Persist & deserialize in config-repository

**File:** `db/config-repository.ts`.

- In `saveProvider()` (~L299–428): when building the provider upsert row, set
  `piAiProvider: config.pi_ai_provider ?? null`. When building each model row
  (the model upsert/replace loop), set `piAiModelId: cfg.pi_ai_model_id ?? null`.
- In `rowToProviderConfig()` (~L523–647): read the provider row's
  `piAiProvider` back into `pi_ai_provider` (omit/undefined when null), and read
  each model row's `piAiModelId` back into the model config's `pi_ai_model_id`.
- Mirror the existing nullable-field handling (these are plaintext, **not**
  encrypted — do not run them through the API-key encryption path).

**Verify:** add a config-repository round-trip test (save a provider with
`pi_ai_provider` + a model `pi_ai_model_id`, reload, assert both survive). Use
the existing repo test pattern under `db/__tests__/`.

### T1.4 — Frontend: provider + model editors and API mapping

**Files:** `packages/frontend/src/`.

- `lib/api.ts`: add `pi_ai_provider?: string` to the `Provider` interface
  (~L157+); include it in the `getProviders()` mapping (~L1653+) and in the
  `saveProvider()` request body (~L1718+). The per-model object is
  `Record<string, any>` and passes `pi_ai_model_id` through automatically — no
  interface change needed for models, but confirm the save path forwards the
  full model object.
- `components/providers/ProviderAdvancedEditor.tsx`: add a "pi-ai Provider" text
  input bound to `provider.pi_ai_provider`.
- `components/providers/ProviderModelsEditor.tsx`: add a per-model "pi-ai Model
  ID" text input bound to each model's `pi_ai_model_id`.
- Follow the `AGENTS.md` frontend rules (no CSS imports into `.tsx`; assets via
  ES6 imports; Tailwind built via `@tailwindcss/cli`). Match the existing input
  components/styling already used in those editors.

**Verify:** `bun run typecheck` (frontend workspace too). Manual: the field
shows in the provider editor and a saved value round-trips (covered fully once
the backend is wired in T1.1–T1.3).

### T1.5 — Create `beta/pi-ai-utils.ts` (shared utilities)

**New file:** `beta/pi-ai-utils.ts`. Source the behaviour from `run.ts` on the
PoC branch and from `oauth-transformer.ts` on `main`.

Export three functions (signatures per `DESIGN.md` → Shared Infrastructure):

- **`resolveBaseUrl(apiBaseUrl, upstreamApi, incomingApiType)`** — resolves the
  `string | Record<string, string>` union (when a record: key first by the
  upstream pi-ai API, then by known Plexus aliases for that upstream API, then
  `"default"`, then first value), then applies the SDK base-URL rule:
  strip a trailing bare `/v\d+` **only** for `anthropic-messages` (the Anthropic
  SDK appends `/v1` itself); preserve the full URL for all other API types.
  This logic is currently inlined in the PoC `run.ts` — lift it here. Do not use
  the client route's `incomingApiType` as the primary key: a chat-completions
  request can route to an Anthropic, Responses, or Gemini upstream via pi-ai.
- **`buildReasoningOptions(piApi, piModelId, effort?)`** — when `effort` is
  present, delegate to `buildThinkingOptions`. When absent, explicitly disable
  thinking per provider: `{ thinkingEnabled: false }` for `anthropic-messages`,
  `{ thinking: { enabled: false } }` for `google-generative-ai`, `{}` for the
  OpenAI family. (Mirrors what `streamSimple` does internally; prevents silent
  thinking-token spend.)
- **`buildPiAiModel(providerConfig, piAiProvider, piAiModelId, apiType)`** —
  call pi-ai `getModel(piAiProvider, piAiModelId)`, then return a shallow copy
  with `baseUrl` overridden to `resolveBaseUrl(providerConfig.api_base_url,
  piModel.api, apiType)`. This is the canonical "give me a ready-to-call pi-ai Model".

**Verify:** unit-test each function: `resolveBaseUrl` for the anthropic strip
vs. preserve cases and the record-union resolution; `buildReasoningOptions` for
the three providers with and without effort.

### T1.6 — Move `buildThinkingOptions` to the shared module

**Files:** `transformers/oauth/oauth-transformer.ts`, `beta/pi-ai-utils.ts`.

- Move the **definition** of `buildThinkingOptions`
  (oauth-transformer.ts:44) into `beta/pi-ai-utils.ts` and export it.
- In `oauth-transformer.ts`, replace the local definition with a re-export /
  import from `beta/pi-ai-utils.ts` so existing callers keep working
  (backward-compatible; `DESIGN.md` calls the current cross-import a "layering
  violation" and wants the shared module to own it).

**Verify:** `bun run typecheck`; existing oauth-transformer tests still pass
unchanged.

### T1.7 — Export `jsonSchemaToTypeBox`

**File:** `transformers/oauth/type-mappers.ts`.

- The function exists **unexported** at `type-mappers.ts:234`. Add `export` so
  the beta inbound parsers (M2–M5) can import it, matching the PoC import path
  (`import { jsonSchemaToTypeBox } from '../transformers/oauth/type-mappers'`).
- Do not change its behaviour. (Optional, defer unless trivial: relocate to a
  more neutral module — but exporting in place is sufficient and lower-risk.)

**Verify:** `bun run typecheck`; a smoke unit test importing it from the new
export path.

### T1.8 — Startup registry validation (non-fatal)

**Files:** `config.ts` (`hydrateConfig`, ~L1004) or a startup check consumed by
the executor.

- For each provider with `pi_ai_provider` set, and each of its models with
  `pi_ai_model_id` set, attempt `getModel(pi_ai_provider, pi_ai_model_id)`.
  `getModel` **throws** for unknown registry pairs (`DESIGN.md` → registry
  coverage).
- On failure, **log a warning, do not throw** — the pi-ai registry can lag new
  model releases. Runtime handling is path-specific: beta routes treat the pair
  as invalid for beta candidate filtering, while `/v1/...` inference routes do
  not inspect these hints. Catch the throw per pair.

**Verify:** unit test — a config with a bogus `pi_ai_model_id` hydrates without
error and emits a warning (assert via the logger mock).

## Open decisions

- **Where startup validation lives** (`hydrateConfig` vs. a dedicated
  startup hook in the executor). Recommended: do it in `hydrateConfig` so it
  runs once at config load and is covered by config tests. Owner: `DESIGN.md`
  → "pi-ai model registry coverage".
- **Relocating `jsonSchemaToTypeBox`** vs. exporting in place. Recommended:
  export in place (T1.7) to minimise churn; revisit during M6 cleanup.

## Test plan (M1)

- `config.ts` schema: both fields optional + string-typed (T1.1).
- `config-repository` round-trip for both fields (T1.3).
- `pi-ai-utils`: `resolveBaseUrl` (anthropic strip vs. preserve; record union),
  `buildReasoningOptions` (3 providers × effort/no-effort) (T1.5).
- `jsonSchemaToTypeBox` import smoke test (T1.7).
- Registry validation warns, does not throw (T1.8).
- Migration lints clean (T1.2).

## Risks / gotchas

- **Migrations are CI-gated.** Use `--name add_pi_ai_hint`; never edit the
  generated file; never run `drizzle-kit` directly.
- **Two dialects.** The postgres and sqlite schemas must both get the columns,
  or the migration generator / runtime will diverge.
- **`pi_model` vs `pi_ai_*` confusion.** They are different fields at different
  levels. Touching `pi_model` is out of scope.
- **`getModel` throws on miss.** The startup check must wrap each call in
  try/catch and downgrade to a warning (T1.8) — a thrown error here would
  prevent Plexus from starting.
- **Global pi-ai mock in tests.** `@earendil-works/pi-ai` is mocked in
  `test/vitest.setup.ts`; the mock's `getModel`/`getModels` shape must cover any
  fields `buildPiAiModel`/validation read (`baseUrl`, `api`). Extend the mock if
  a field is missing rather than re-mocking in the test file.

---

# M2 — Stage 1: `/beta/v1/chat/completions` + the full pi-ai executor

Source: https://github.com/mcowger/plexus/blob/main/docs/plexus-piai-plan/M2.md

# M2 — Stage 1: `/beta/v1/chat/completions` + the full pi-ai executor

**Depends on:** M1. **Blocks:** M3, M4, M5 (they reuse the executor and the beta
route pattern). M6 Stage-1 production promotion depends on this.

This is the keystone milestone. It builds the **stage-agnostic executor**
(`beta/pi-ai-executor.ts`) with the *complete* Dispatcher integration the PoC
left out, plus the OpenAI inbound/outbound and the first beta route. M3–M5 then
become "write a parser + serialiser + route" because the hard part lives here.

Design references: `DESIGN.md` → "The Beta Parallel Path Pattern", "Stage 1",
"Full Dispatcher Integration Design", "Raw response capture", "Known Issues and
Gaps". PoC reference (read, don't build on):
`feat/piai-parallel-chat-completions-inference-path:src/beta/{run.ts,openai-to-context.ts,context-to-openai.ts,index.ts}`.

## Goal & exit criteria

Done when:

- `beta/pi-ai-executor.ts` implements the full failover loop with cooldown
  pre-check, concurrency acquire/release (including release-after-stream),
  per-attempt timeout kept active through streaming completion, stall detection
  (TTFB for streaming via a real timeout race), retry classification, usage
  recording, explicit quota recording, and debug logging.
- `beta/openai-to-context.ts` and `beta/context-to-openai.ts` exist and pass
  unit tests for all message/event shapes.
- `POST /beta/v1/chat/completions` is registered (via `beta/index.ts` →
  `registerBetaRoutes`, wired into `routes/inference/index.ts` inside the
  protected block) and fails closed with HTTP 400 when no registry-valid
  beta-compatible candidate remains.
- Raw upstream response capture for debug works for both streaming and
  non-streaming (global `fetch` tap, recommended approach).
- Integration test: mock pi-ai `stream`/`complete` with known event sequences;
  assert SSE output and `UsageRecord` shape.
- Gates pass: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, `bun run format:check`.

## Tasks

### T2.1 — Inbound parser `beta/openai-to-context.ts`

**New file.** Port and harden from the PoC. Converts OpenAI chat-completions
JSON → pi-ai `Context` + a `ProviderStreamOptions` fragment.

Must handle (`DESIGN.md` → Stage 1 inbound):
- `system` and `developer` roles → collapsed into `context.systemPrompt`
  (multiple system messages concatenated with `\n\n`; document this).
- `user` messages: text and base64 image content (`ImageContent`). **URL image
  content: keep rejecting with an error for now** (open decision below).
- `assistant` messages: text + tool calls (`ToolCallContent`).
- `tool` role messages → `ToolResultMessage`.
- Tool definitions via the now-exported `jsonSchemaToTypeBox` (from M1.7),
  imported from `transformers/oauth/type-mappers`.
- Options fragment: `temperature`, `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens`
  (→ `maxTokens`), `tool_choice`, `parallel_tool_calls`, and `reasoning_effort`
  → routed through `buildReasoningOptions` (M1.5) at execute time. **Use the
  `stream()`/`complete()` `ProviderStreamOptions` path, never
  `streamSimple()`** — the latter drops `toolChoice`/`parallelToolCalls`
  (`DESIGN.md` → "Why `stream()` and not `streamSimple()`").

**Verify:** unit tests covering every role combination, multi-part content,
tool defs, and reasoning_effort pass-through (`DESIGN.md` → Stage 1 testing).

### T2.2 — Outbound serialiser `beta/context-to-openai.ts`

**New file.** Port from the PoC. Converts `AssistantMessage` →
`OpenAIChatCompletion` and `AssistantMessageEvent` → `OpenAIChatChunk`, plus
`chunkToSSE` (emits `data: {...}\n\n`) and a terminal `data: [DONE]\n\n`.

Must handle (`DESIGN.md` → Stage 1 outbound):
- Text, thinking/reasoning (`reasoning_content`).
- Tool calls with the correct **0-based `tool_calls` array index**, kept
  separate from the content-block index (this was a real PoC subtlety).
- Usage field mapping.
- Stop-reason mapping.
- Error surfacing: when `AssistantMessage.stopReason === 'error'`, surface
  `message.errorMessage` as content so the caller sees the upstream error.

**Verify:** unit tests for all event types, tool-call index computation, usage
mapping, stop-reason mapping, and the error path.

### T2.3 — The executor `beta/pi-ai-executor.ts`

**New file.** This replaces the PoC's `run.ts` orchestrator with the
production design. Implement the interface and failover loop from `DESIGN.md` →
"Full Dispatcher Integration Design" (read that section in full; it contains
the loop pseudocode).

Interface (per design):
```
interface PiAiExecutorInput {
  requestId, incomingApiType, modelAlias, context, streamOptions,
  streaming, request, usageStorage, quotaEnforcer?, signal?, onSuccess
}
interface PiAiExecutorResult { response?: unknown; stream?: AsyncIterable<string> }
```

The executor is **wire-format-agnostic** — it never imports OpenAI/Anthropic
types. The route handler passes the parser output (`context`, `streamOptions`,
`streaming`) and the serialiser as callbacks. (Concretely: the executor takes
serialiser callbacks for non-streaming and streaming, or returns the raw
`AssistantMessage`/event stream and the route applies the serialiser — pick one
shape and keep it consistent for M3–M5. Recommended: executor takes
`serializeMessage` and `serializeEvents` callbacks so streaming TTFB/usage
tapping stays inside the executor.)

Sub-tasks (each maps to a verified symbol — file:line from baseline):

- **T2.3a — Candidate resolution & key policy.**
  `candidates = await Router.resolveCandidates(modelAlias, incomingApiType)`
  (`services/router.ts:267`); fall back to `[await Router.resolve(...)]`
  (`router.ts:398`) if empty; then `applyKeyAccessPolicy(...)`
  (`dispatcher.ts:1452` — currently private to Dispatcher; **open decision**
  below on how to share it). After key policy, filter to **beta-compatible**
  candidates only: both hints must be present and `getModel(pi_ai_provider,
  pi_ai_model_id)` must succeed. If the filtered list is empty, return the
  route's protocol-shaped 400/failed response. Do not include non-hint or
  registry-invalid candidates in the beta failover loop, and do not fall back to
  the legacy Transformer path.
- **T2.3b — Per-candidate guards.** For each candidate, in order:
  abort check → `createAttemptTimeout(signal, route.config.timeoutMs)`
  (`dispatcher.ts:2429`) → `CooldownManager.isProviderHealthy(provider, model)`
  (`cooldown-manager.ts:261`); on unhealthy, `appendSkippedAttempt`
  (`dispatcher.ts:1339`) and continue → `ConcurrencyTracker.acquire(provider,
  model)` (`concurrency-tracker.ts:33`); on false, skip + append + continue.
- **T2.3c — Build the call.** Read `route.config.pi_ai_provider` and
  `route.modelConfig?.pi_ai_model_id`; the candidate filter should already have
  removed missing or registry-invalid hints, but keep a defensive fail-closed
  check. Build the model with `buildPiAiModel(...)` (M1.5), which resolves
  configured base URLs by upstream pi-ai API (`piModel.api`), not by the client
  route type. Assemble `ProviderStreamOptions`:
  `{ ...streamOptions, ...buildReasoningOptions(...), apiKey: route.config.api_key,
  headers: route.config.headers, signal: attemptTimeout.signal, onPayload: (p)
  => debug.addTransformedRequest(requestId, p) }`.
- **T2.3d — Stall config.** Resolve global stall config merged with route
  overrides (`route.config.stallTtfbMs` etc.); the HTTP path uses
  `wireStallDetection` / `addStallConfig` (`utils/stall.ts:122`). For pi-ai
  there is **no `probeStreamingStart`** (it needs a raw `Response`); implement
  the TTFB equivalent in the stream generator (T2.4).
- **T2.3e — Invoke pi-ai.** Non-streaming: `await complete(piModel, context,
  options)`. Streaming: `stream(piModel, context, options)` returning an
  `AsyncIterable<AssistantMessageEvent>`, wrapped by the SSE generator (T2.4).
- **T2.3f — Success path.** Non-streaming: after `complete()` returns, call
  `CooldownManager.markProviderSuccess` (`cooldown-manager.ts:228`),
  `appendSuccessAttempt` (`dispatcher.ts:1356`), release slot,
  `attemptTimeout.cleanup()`, then `await onSuccess(message)`. Streaming:
  return the wrapped stream without marking success, releasing concurrency, or
  cleaning up timeout yet. The stream wrapper owns those actions after a
  successful terminal event; it must also own failure/cancel cleanup if the
  stream errors.
- **T2.3g — Failure path.** Compute `effectiveErr` (timeout vs. raw) via
  `attemptTimeout.isTimedOut()`; if `signal?.aborted` throw `buildCancelledError`
  (`dispatcher.ts:2461`) — client disconnect is **never** retried.
  Call `markProviderFailure` (`cooldown-manager.ts:175`) or, for stalls,
  `markProviderStallFailure` (`cooldown-manager.ts:93`) **only if**
  `route.config.stall_cooldown` is set (else skip cooldown for stalls, same as
  HTTP path). For failures before a stream is returned to the route, release the
  slot and clean up the attempt timeout here. For failures from an already
  returned streaming wrapper, the wrapper performs release/cleanup exactly once.
  Compute `canRetry = failoverEnabled && i < last && isRetryable(effectiveErr)`;
  `appendFailureAttempt` (`dispatcher.ts:1372`); if retry,
  `saveIntermediateError` (`dispatcher.ts:203`) and continue; else
  `throw buildAllTargetsFailedError(...)` (`dispatcher.ts:1395`).
- **T2.3h — `isRetryable(err)`.** Retryable = signal not aborted AND
  (`AbortError` from attempt timeout → `upstream_timeout`, OR network errors
  ECONNREFUSED/ETIMEDOUT, OR pi-ai HTTP errors surfacing as 5xx). Non-retryable
  otherwise. (`DESIGN.md` → Stage 1 "retryable errors".) For streaming, this
  predicate is additionally gated by whether any client frame has already been
  emitted: retry only before first emitted SSE/NDJSON frame. Use
  `extractPiAiErrorMessage` (`type-mappers.ts:560`) for messages.

**Verify:** unit-test the loop with a mocked Router/Cooldown/Concurrency:
healthy→success, unhealthy→skip→next, acquire-fail→skip, retryable→failover,
non-retryable→throw, all-exhausted→`buildAllTargetsFailedError`, abort→cancelled.

### T2.4 — Streaming generator + TTFB stall + concurrency release

Inside the executor (the function the design calls `buildSSEStream`):

- Wrap `for await (const event of eventStream)`; start a TTFB deadline when
  `stream()` returns. Implement this as a real `Promise.race` around
  `iterator.next()` (or an equivalent helper), not as a wall-clock check inside
  the loop body. If no non-`start` event arrives within `stallConfig.ttfbMs`,
  abort the upstream via the signal and throw a `StallError` that the failover
  loop treats as a stall only if no client frame has been emitted yet
  (`DESIGN.md` → "Stall detection for pi-ai streaming" and "Streaming failure
  boundary").
- Accumulate content blocks + usage as events arrive (for the reconstructed
  debug response, T2.6).
- **Streaming lifecycle in terminal path:** keep concurrency and the per-attempt
  timeout active until the stream terminal event, client cancel, or error. On a
  successful terminal event, mark provider success, append success history,
  save usage, record quota usage, call `onSuccess`, release the slot, clean up
  timeout, and `debug.flush(requestId)`. On error/cancel, release and clean up
  exactly once, save error usage/debug state, and do not retry if a client frame
  has already been emitted.
- Yield serialised frames (`chunkToSSE(...)` + terminal `SSE_DONE`).

**Verify:** unit test a stream that stalls before first content → aborts and is
eligible for failover; a stream that fails after the first client frame does not
retry; a normal stream releases the slot and cleans up timeout exactly once.

### T2.5 — Beta route `beta/index.ts` + wiring

**New file** `beta/index.ts` exporting `registerBetaRoutes(fastify,
usageStorage, quotaEnforcer?)`. Port the route scaffolding from the PoC
`index.ts` but call the new executor.

Handler for `POST /beta/v1/chat/completions`:
1. `requestId = crypto.randomUUID()`; set `x-request-id` header.
2. `debug.startLog(requestId, body, sanitizeHeaders(request.headers))`.
3. Quota: if `quotaEnforcer`, `if (!(await checkQuotaMiddleware(request, reply,
   quotaEnforcer))) return;` (`quota-middleware.ts:18`).
4. Wire abort: `wireUpstreamTimeout` (`utils/timeout.ts:27`) +
   `wireEarlyDisconnectDetection` (`utils/timeout.ts:61`).
5. Parse: `openaiRequestToContext(body)` → `{ context, streamOptions, streaming }`.
6. Call executor; write `result.response` as JSON or pump `result.stream` into a
   `ReadableStream` with SSE headers (PoC pattern).
7. `onSuccess` is a no-op for Stage 1.
8. Error shape: OpenAI `{ error: { message, type } }`.

**Wire into app:** in `routes/inference/index.ts`, inside the protected
`fastify.register(async (protectedRoutes) => {...})` block (after
`registerResponsesRoute`, ~L37), add `await registerBetaRoutes(protectedRoutes,
usageStorage, quotaEnforcer);` so beta inherits auth + bearer auth.

**Verify:** route returns 400 when no registry-valid beta-compatible candidate
remains; returns SSE for `stream:true` and JSON otherwise (integration test,
T2.8).

### T2.6 — Usage recording

The executor populates a `UsageRecord` incrementally (`DESIGN.md` → "Usage
recording"; `types/usage.ts` / `services/usage-storage.ts`) and records quota
usage after costs are finalized:
- `emitStartedAsync(record)` at request start (`usage-storage.ts:176`).
- `emitUpdatedAsync({ requestId, provider, selectedModelName, canonicalModelName })`
  after route resolution (`usage-storage.ts:180`).
- `saveRequest(record)` after stream completes / non-streaming response built
  (`usage-storage.ts:120`).
- Fields from pi-ai: `tokensInput/Output/Cached/CacheWrite` from
  `AssistantMessage.usage`; `costInput/Output/.../Total` from
  `calculateCost(piModel, usage)`; `costSource: 'pi-ai'`; `finishReason` from
  `stopReason`; `toolCallsCount` = count of `ToolCallContent` blocks; `ttftMs` =
  start→first non-`start` event; `durationMs` = total; `attemptCount` /
  `retryHistory` from the loop. `responseStatus` ∈
  `success|error|timeout|cancelled`.
- After `saveRequest(record)`, if `quotaEnforcer` and `(request as any).keyName`
  are present, call `recordQuotaUsage(keyName, record, quotaEnforcer)` from
  `services/quota/quota-middleware.ts`. `saveRequest()` alone does not consume
  quota.

**Verify:** integration test asserts the saved `UsageRecord` matches expected
token/cost/finish/ttft fields for a known mocked event sequence, and that quota
usage is recorded once with the finalized token/cost values.

### T2.7 — Debug logging + raw-response capture

- Calls: `debug.startLog` (route, T2.5), `debug.setProviderForRequest(requestId,
  provider)` (`debug-manager.ts:103`) right after route resolution,
  `debug.addTransformedRequest` via `onPayload`, `debug.addTransformedResponse`
  for non-streaming and (for streaming) the **reconstructed** `AssistantMessage`
  after `done`, `debug.flush` in the generator `finally`.
- **Raw upstream response capture:** pi-ai does not expose the raw body.
  Implement the **global `fetch` monkey-patch** (recommended in `DESIGN.md` →
  "Raw response capture"): at server startup, before registering beta routes,
  wrap `globalThis.fetch`. Correlate the in-flight request to `requestId` via
  `AsyncLocalStorage` set in the `onPayload` callback. On response: for
  non-streaming clone+buffer the body → `DebugManager.addRawResponse`; for
  streaming wrap the body in a `TransformStream` that copies chunks to the debug
  log as they pass through (**not** `tee()` — avoids upstream backpressure).
  Only tap when debug is active for the current request.

**Verify:** with debug enabled, a non-streaming call records both transformed
request (via `onPayload`) and raw response; a streaming call records the
reconstructed response after `done`.

### T2.8 — Tests

- Unit: `openai-to-context` (T2.1), `context-to-openai` (T2.2), executor loop
  (T2.3), stream/TTFB/release (T2.4).
- Integration (in `__tests__/`, per the existing pattern): mock pi-ai `stream`
  and `complete` with known `AssistantMessageEvent` sequences; assert SSE output
  byte-shape and the `UsageRecord`. Remember pi-ai is **globally mocked** in
  `test/vitest.setup.ts` — extend that mock's event shapes rather than
  re-mocking; reset via `resetForTesting()` in `beforeEach`; use `registerSpy`.

## Open decisions

- **Sharing `applyKeyAccessPolicy`** (currently private on `Dispatcher`,
  `dispatcher.ts:1452`). Options: (a) extract to a shared helper both
  Dispatcher and executor import; (b) duplicate the small policy in the
  executor. Recommended: (a) extract — avoids drift. Owner: `DESIGN.md` →
  Full Dispatcher Integration / failover loop.
- **Executor return shape**: serialiser-callbacks-inside vs. raw-message-out.
  Recommended: serialiser callbacks inside the executor so TTFB timing and
  reconstructed-debug stay co-located. Lock this in M2; M3–M5 must follow it.
- **URL image content**: keep the error (Stage 1). Revisit globally when a
  backend known to support URL images is configured. Owner: `DESIGN.md` →
  Stage 1 inbound "Gaps to close".
- **Raw capture approach**: global `fetch` tap (recommended) vs. local proxy.
  Pick the tap; it's simplest and Plexus is the only `fetch` caller in-process.

## Risks / gotchas

- **`streamSimple` option loss** — must use `stream()`/`complete()` with
  `ProviderStreamOptions`, or `tool_choice`/`parallel_tool_calls` vanish
  silently (`DESIGN.md` → known issues). The PoC's `run.ts` header comment says
  it uses `streamSimple`, but the design mandates `stream()`; **follow the
  design, not the PoC comment.**
- **Base-URL stripping** — only `anthropic-messages` strips trailing `/v\d+`
  (handled by `resolveBaseUrl` from M1). A new API type could need different
  handling; validate against a live provider.
- **Concurrency leak on streaming** — release must be in both `finally` and
  `catch` of the generator, never before consumption ends.
- **Timeout leak on streaming** — per-attempt timeout cleanup must also wait for
  stream completion/error; cleaning it up immediately after `stream()` returns
  leaves hung streams unbounded.
- **Post-first-frame retry corruption** — retrying after any SSE/NDJSON frame has
  reached the client mixes providers in one stream. Retry streaming attempts only
  before the first emitted client frame.
- **Quota accounting** — `saveRequest()` does not consume quota. Call
  `recordQuotaUsage()` after costs are calculated.
- **Stall semantics** — respect `route.config.stall_cooldown`: when false, a
  stall failure must **not** trigger a cooldown.
- **Client disconnect never retried** — gate retry on `!signal.aborted`.
- **`getModel` panics on registry miss** — M1.8 validates at startup, but the
  beta executor must still filter registry-invalid candidates before execution.
  If no valid beta-compatible candidates remain, fail closed with the route's
  protocol-shaped error; do not fall through to the legacy Transformer path.
- **Raw-capture global state** — the `fetch` tap touches process-global state;
  scope it to debug-active requests via `AsyncLocalStorage` and ensure tests
  don't leak the patched `fetch` between cases.

---

# M3 — Stage 2: `/beta/v1/messages` (Anthropic-compatible)

Source: https://github.com/mcowger/plexus/blob/main/docs/plexus-piai-plan/M3.md

# M3 — Stage 2: `/beta/v1/messages` (Anthropic-compatible)

**Depends on:** M2 (executor + beta pattern). **Blocks:** M6 Stage-2 production promotion.

Anthropic is structurally different from OpenAI chat-completions, but the
executor from M2 is wire-format-agnostic, so this milestone is almost entirely
*parser + serialiser + route*. The executor, failover, cooldown, concurrency,
stall, usage, debug, and raw-capture are all inherited unchanged — only
`incomingApiType: 'messages'` and the error-shape differ.

Design references: `DESIGN.md` → "Stage 2". Existing code to study (do not
import wholesale): `transformers/anthropic/request-parser.ts`
(`parseAnthropicRequest`), `transformers/anthropic/stream-formatter.ts`
(`formatAnthropicStream`), `getThinkLevel` (`transformers/utils.ts:43`).

## Goal & exit criteria

Done when:

- `beta/anthropic-to-context.ts` converts Anthropic messages JSON → pi-ai
  `Context` + `ProviderStreamOptions`, including thinking blocks in history.
- `beta/context-to-anthropic.ts` emits the Anthropic non-streaming response and
  the full Anthropic SSE event sequence from `AssistantMessage` /
  `AssistantMessageEvent`.
- `POST /beta/v1/messages` is registered in `beta/index.ts`, uses the M2
  executor with `incomingApiType: 'messages'`, and returns Anthropic-shaped
  errors.
- Unit + integration tests pass (SSE byte-shape vs. the Anthropic protocol).
- Gates: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, `bun run format:check`.

## Tasks

### T3.1 — Inbound parser `beta/anthropic-to-context.ts`

**New file.** Mirrors `openai-to-context.ts` in structure, speaks Anthropic.
Cross-check every mapping against the existing `parseAnthropicRequest()` so
behaviour matches the legacy path (`DESIGN.md` → Stage 2 inbound).

- **System prompt:** accept `string` and `ContentBlock[]`. For the array form,
  concatenate text blocks with `\n\n`. **Cache-control on system blocks:** see
  open decision — for now, pass through if pi-ai propagates it, else strip.
- **User messages:** content arrays — `text` → `TextContent`; `image` with
  `source.type === "base64"` → `ImageContent`; `image` with `source.type ===
  "url"` → same decision as Stage 1 (reject for now).
- **Assistant messages (history):** preserve `thinking` blocks. pi-ai
  `AssistantMessage.content` supports `ThinkingContent` (`{ type: "thinking",
  thinking }`). Anthropic **requires** thinking blocks in history when extended
  thinking is active, so they must survive the round-trip.
- **Tool use/result:** `tool_use` (assistant) → `ToolCallContent`;
  `tool_result` (user) → `ToolResultMessage`.
- **Tool definitions:** Anthropic `{ name, description, input_schema }`; map
  `input_schema` through `jsonSchemaToTypeBox` (exported in M1.7).
- **Reasoning:** Anthropic uses `{ thinking: { type: "enabled", budget_tokens:
  N } }`. Map `budget_tokens` → an effort string via `getThinkLevel`
  (`transformers/utils.ts:43`), then feed `buildReasoningOptions` (M1.5).

**Verify:** unit tests — multi-block system prompts, thinking blocks in history,
tool use/result interleaving, thinking-config mapping.

### T3.2 — Outbound serialiser `beta/context-to-anthropic.ts`

**New file.** Study `formatAnthropicStream()` in
`transformers/anthropic/stream-formatter.ts` for edge cases (multiple tool
calls, interleaved thinking + text) before finalising.

- **Non-streaming:** `{ id, type: "message", role: "assistant", model, content:
  [...], stop_reason, stop_sequence: null, usage }`. Content order: `thinking`
  blocks first (if present), then `text`, then `tool_use`. Stop-reason map:
  `stop`→`end_turn`, `toolUse`→`tool_use`, `length`→`max_tokens`. Usage:
  `{ input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens,
  cache_creation_input_tokens }`.
- **Streaming (Anthropic SSE):** consume `AssistantMessageEvent` and emit
  (`DESIGN.md` → Stage 2 streaming, full event list):
  - `start` → `message_start` (empty content, initial usage if available).
  - `text_delta` → lazy `content_block_start {type:"text"}` then
    `content_block_delta {type:"text_delta"}`.
  - `thinking_delta` → lazy `content_block_start {type:"thinking"}` then
    `content_block_delta {type:"thinking_delta"}`.
  - `toolcall_delta` → on first delta `content_block_start
    {type:"tool_use", id, name, input:{}}` then `content_block_delta
    {type:"input_json_delta", partial_json}`.
  - `done` → `content_block_stop` for any open block, then `message_delta
    {stop_reason, stop_sequence:null}` with final usage, then `message_stop`.
  - `error` → `message_delta` with `stop_reason:"error"` and close.

**Verify:** unit tests for the full SSE sequence (text-only; thinking+text;
single tool; multi-tool) and the non-streaming shape.

### T3.3 — Route `POST /beta/v1/messages`

**File:** `beta/index.ts` (extend `registerBetaRoutes`).

- Same scaffold as `/beta/v1/chat/completions`: requestId + `x-request-id`,
  `debug.startLog`, quota middleware, abort wiring, parse via
  `anthropicRequestToContext`, call the M2 executor with `incomingApiType:
  'messages'`, write JSON or Anthropic SSE.
- **Error shape must be Anthropic:** `{ type: "error", error: { type, message }
  }` — not the OpenAI shape. (Matches the existing `/v1/messages` handler.)
- `onSuccess` is a no-op for Stage 2.

**Verify:** 400 when no registry-valid beta-compatible candidate remains
(Anthropic error shape); SSE vs. JSON by `stream` flag.

### T3.4 — Tests

- Unit: T3.1 and T3.2 cases above.
- Integration: mock pi-ai with a known event sequence and assert the SSE output
  matches the Anthropic streaming protocol. Use the existing
  `anthropic-stream.test.ts` as the reference for expected byte-shape. pi-ai is
  globally mocked (`test/vitest.setup.ts`) — extend, don't re-mock; reset via
  `resetForTesting()`; use `registerSpy`.

## Open decisions

- **Cache-control on system blocks** (Anthropic prompt caching). Determine
  whether pi-ai's Anthropic SDK integration propagates `cache_control` on system
  blocks: if yes, pass the array form through; if no, the `\n\n` concatenation
  is acceptable (pi-ai manages caching at a different level). Owner: `DESIGN.md`
  → "Multi-system-prompt concatenation". **Resolve before finalising T3.1.**
- **URL image content** — same as Stage 1: reject for now.
- **Thinking detection robustness** — `buildThinkingOptions` currently uses
  fragile model-ID `includes()` checks. `DESIGN.md` ("Thinking options for
  non-thinking models") wants this hardened to read `piModel.compat` /
  `piModel.thinkingLevelMap` **before Stage 2 ships to production**. Decide
  whether to harden in this milestone (recommended, since Anthropic is the
  thinking-heavy provider) or track as a follow-up. If hardened, do it in
  `beta/pi-ai-utils.ts` (`buildThinkingOptions`/`buildReasoningOptions`) so all
  stages benefit.

## Risks / gotchas

- **Thinking blocks in history are mandatory** for Anthropic extended thinking —
  dropping them on the inbound side breaks multi-turn thinking conversations.
- **Content ordering** in the non-streaming response (thinking → text →
  tool_use) is part of the Anthropic contract; assert it in tests.
- **SSE event ordering** — Anthropic clients are strict about the
  `message_start` → `content_block_*` → `message_delta` → `message_stop`
  sequence; the lazy `content_block_start` emission must fire before the first
  delta of each block.
- **Error shape divergence** — easy to accidentally reuse the OpenAI error
  helper; the messages route must emit `{ type:"error", error:{...} }`.
- **Executor reuse** — do not fork the executor. If something is missing for
  Anthropic, it belongs in the shared executor (M2), not a Stage-2 copy.

---

# M4 — Stage 3: `/beta/v1/responses` (OpenAI Responses API)

Source: https://github.com/mcowger/plexus/blob/main/docs/plexus-piai-plan/M4.md

# M4 — Stage 3: `/beta/v1/responses` (OpenAI Responses API)

**Depends on:** M2 (executor + beta pattern). **Blocks:** M6 Stage-3 production promotion.

The Responses API has a different input/output shape *and* server-side state
(`previous_response_id`, `conversation`, post-response storage). The executor is
still reused unchanged — the new wrinkle is that **state loading happens in the
route handler before parsing**, and **post-response storage happens via the
executor's `onSuccess` hook** (the first non-trivial use of that hook).

Design references: `DESIGN.md` → "Stage 3" and "Responses API state storage in
beta". Existing code to study/borrow: `routes/inference/responses.ts`
(`normalizeInput` ~L75, `previous_response_id`/`conversation` loading ~L89–129,
`body.store` storage ~L221–231), `ResponsesStorageService`
(`services/responses-storage.ts`: `getResponse:165`, `getConversation:260`,
`storeResponse:88`, `updateConversation:207`), and `ResponsesTransformer`
(`formatStream`/`transformStream` for the exact streaming event sequence).

## Goal & exit criteria

Done when:

- `beta/responses-to-context.ts` converts the (already-concatenated) Responses
  `input` array → pi-ai `Context` + `ProviderStreamOptions`.
- `beta/context-to-responses.ts` emits the Responses non-streaming object and
  the Responses streaming event sequence.
- `POST /beta/v1/responses` is registered, loads `previous_response_id` /
  `conversation` context **before** parsing (reusing the existing handler's
  logic), calls the M2 executor with `incomingApiType: 'responses'`, and stores
  the response via `onSuccess` when `body.store !== false`.
- Unit + integration tests pass.
- Gates: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, `bun run format:check`.

## Tasks

### T4.1 — Inbound parser `beta/responses-to-context.ts`

**New file.** Converts the Responses `input` array → pi-ai `Context`
(`DESIGN.md` → Stage 3 inbound). By the time this runs, `body.input` already
contains the full concatenated history (the route does state loading first — see
T4.3), so this parser is pure shape-mapping.

- **Input normalization:** borrow `normalizeInput()` logic from `responses.ts`
  (~L75) for the string → array conversion. Items are `type: "message"` with
  `role` + `content[]` whose entries have types `input_text`, `input_image`,
  `output_text`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`.
- **Message mapping:** `role:"user"` + `input_text` → `UserMessage`;
  `role:"assistant"` + `output_text` → assistant history; `role:"assistant"` +
  `tool_call` → assistant with `ToolCallContent`; tool-result items →
  `ToolResultMessage`.
- **System:** no top-level `system`; collect `role:"system"` items into
  `context.systemPrompt`.
- **Tools:** `jsonSchemaToTypeBox` (M1.7).
- **Reasoning:** Responses uses `reasoning: { effort, summary }`; map `effort`
  via `buildReasoningOptions` (M1.5). Track whether `summary` was requested so
  the serialiser can emit reasoning summaries (T4.2).

**Verify:** unit tests — string input, message/tool_call/tool_result mapping,
system collection, reasoning effort pass-through.

### T4.2 — Outbound serialiser `beta/context-to-responses.ts`

**New file.** Study `ResponsesTransformer.formatStream()` and
`transformStream()` for the exact event sequence before implementing
(`DESIGN.md` → Stage 3 outbound).

- **Non-streaming:** `{ id, object: "response", status: "completed", model,
  output: [...], usage: { input_tokens, output_tokens, ... } }`. Output items:
  text block → `{ type:"message", role:"assistant", content:[{ type:
  "output_text", text }] }`; reasoning content → `{ type:"reasoning", summary:[{
  type:"summary_text", text }] }` (only when summary requested); tool calls →
  `{ type:"function_call", call_id, name, arguments }`.
- **Streaming:** the Responses event schema is verbose. Emit the sequence
  `response.created` → `response.output_item.added` →
  `response.content_part.added` → `response.output_text.delta` →
  `response.output_text.done` → `response.content_part.done` →
  `response.output_item.done` → `response.completed`. Match the exact ordering
  and ids used by `ResponsesTransformer.formatStream()`.

**Verify:** unit tests — non-streaming shape (text, reasoning-summary, tool
call) and the full streaming event sequence.

### T4.3 — Route `POST /beta/v1/responses` (with state)

**File:** `beta/index.ts` (extend `registerBetaRoutes`; it will need a
`ResponsesStorageService` instance — construct one like `responses.ts:24`).

Handler order (mirror `responses.ts`, then diverge to the executor):
1. requestId + `x-request-id`; `debug.startLog`; quota middleware; abort wiring.
2. **State loading BEFORE parsing** (`responses.ts` ~L89–129): if
   `previous_response_id`, `getResponse(...)`; if missing → Responses-shaped
   error. If `conversation`, `getConversation(...)`; prepend its items to
   `normalizeInput(body.input)`. After this, `body.input` holds full history.
3. Parse via `responsesToContext(body)` (T4.1).
4. Call the M2 executor with `incomingApiType: 'responses'` and an **`onSuccess`
   hook** that performs post-response storage: when `body.store !== false`
   (note: existing handler also guards `!body.stream` for storage — preserve
   that), call `responsesStorage.storeResponse(formattedResponse, body)` and, if
   `body.conversation`, `responsesStorage.updateConversation(...)`
   (`responses.ts` ~L221–231). The hook receives the `AssistantMessage`; build
   the stored response object from it (reuse T4.2's non-streaming serialiser).
5. Write JSON or Responses SSE.
6. Error shape: OpenAI Responses error shape (as in `responses.ts`).

**Verify:** `previous_response_id` not-found → correct error; a stored
non-streaming response is retrievable via the existing `getResponse` path;
conversation prepend works.

### T4.4 — Tests

- Unit: T4.1 and T4.2 cases.
- Integration: mock pi-ai event sequence; assert Responses SSE output and the
  non-streaming object; assert `onSuccess` stores when `store !== false` and
  skips when `store === false`. pi-ai globally mocked — extend, don't re-mock;
  reset via `resetForTesting()`; `registerSpy`.

## Open decisions

- **Storage of streaming responses.** The existing handler stores only
  non-streaming (`body.store !== false && !body.stream`, `responses.ts:221`).
  Decide whether the beta path should additionally store streaming responses
  using the reconstructed `AssistantMessage` (the executor already reconstructs
  one for debug, T2.6/T2.7). Recommended: **match existing behaviour** (store
  non-streaming only) to stay zero-regression; revisit later. Owner: `DESIGN.md`
  → "Responses API state storage in beta".
- **`onSuccess` signature** — it receives the `AssistantMessage`. Confirm the
  M2 executor passes enough context (model name, usage) for `storeResponse` to
  build a complete stored object; if not, widen the hook payload in M2 rather
  than reaching into executor internals here.
- **URL image / reasoning-detection** — same standing decisions as Stages 1–2.

## Risks / gotchas

- **State loading must precede parsing.** If you parse `body.input` before
  prepending conversation/previous-response history, the model loses context.
  Order matters (T4.3 step 2 before step 3).
- **`onSuccess` is the only storage path in beta.** Unlike the legacy handler
  (which stores after `handleResponse`), the beta path has no `handleResponse`;
  forgetting to wire `onSuccess` silently drops persistence.
- **Responses streaming is the most verbose schema** of all stages — get the
  event ordering and `output_index`/`content_index` bookkeeping right by
  matching `ResponsesTransformer.formatStream()`.
- **Don't double-load state.** The beta route loads state itself; it must
  bypass `Dispatcher.dispatch()` entirely (executor path), so there's no second
  loader to coordinate with.
- **Executor reuse** — as with M3, missing capability belongs in the shared
  executor, not a Stage-3 fork.

---

# M5 — Stage 4: `/v1beta/models/:model:generateContent` (Gemini-compatible)

Source: https://github.com/mcowger/plexus/blob/main/docs/plexus-piai-plan/M5.md

# M5 — Stage 4: `/v1beta/models/:model:generateContent` (Gemini-compatible)

**Depends on:** M2 (executor + beta pattern). **Blocks:** M6 Stage-4 production promotion.

Gemini is the most structurally distinct surface: the model name is URL-encoded
with an action suffix, streaming is detected from the URL (not the body),
streaming uses **NDJSON** (one JSON object per line) instead of SSE, and tool
results are encoded as `functionResponse` parts inside a `user`-role turn (the
trickiest mapping in the whole project). The executor is still reused unchanged;
the only executor-facing differences are `incomingApiType: 'gemini'`, the
`streaming` flag derived from the URL, and NDJSON framing on the serialiser
side.

Design references: `DESIGN.md` → "Stage 4". Existing code to study:
`routes/inference/gemini.ts` (route + action parsing: `:modelWithAction` at L28,
`streamGenerateContent` detection at L97), `transformers/gemini/`
(`request-parser.ts`, `part-mapper.ts`, `response-formatter.ts`,
`stream-formatter.ts`, `stream-transformer.ts`).

## Goal & exit criteria

Done when:

- `beta/gemini-to-context.ts` converts Gemini `contents` → pi-ai `Context` +
  `ProviderStreamOptions`, including the `functionResponse` → `ToolResultMessage`
  mapping.
- `beta/context-to-gemini.ts` emits the Gemini non-streaming object and **NDJSON
  streaming** frames.
- A beta Gemini route is registered (URL-encoded model + action), derives
  `streaming` from the `:streamGenerateContent` suffix, calls the M2 executor
  with `incomingApiType: 'gemini'`, and emits NDJSON for streaming.
- Unit + integration tests pass.
- Gates: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`, `bun run format:check`.

## Tasks

### T5.1 — Inbound parser `beta/gemini-to-context.ts`

**New file.** Cross-check mappings against `transformers/gemini/request-parser.ts`
and `part-mapper.ts` (`DESIGN.md` → Stage 4 inbound).

- **System instruction:** `systemInstruction.parts[].text` →
  `context.systemPrompt`.
- **Contents:** each `{ role: "user" | "model", parts: [...] }`. `role:"model"`
  → assistant. Parts: `text` → `TextContent`; `inlineData` (base64) →
  `ImageContent`; `functionCall` → `ToolCallContent`; `functionResponse` →
  `ToolResultMessage`. **The tricky case:** Gemini encodes tool results as
  `functionResponse` parts *inside a `user`-role turn* — detect these and split
  them out into `ToolResultMessage`s rather than treating the turn as a plain
  user message.
- **Tools:** Gemini `functionDeclarations` → pi-ai `Tool` via
  `jsonSchemaToTypeBox` (M1.7). Gemini uses OpenAPI-style schemas (mostly
  compatible; watch for type-name differences).
- **Reasoning:** Gemini 2.5+ uses `generationConfig.thinkingConfig`. Map to
  `buildReasoningOptions('google-generative-ai', ...)`. For thinking-level
  models (2.5 Pro/Flash), map the level string to the effort string.
- **Generation config:** map `generationConfig.temperature`, `maxOutputTokens`
  (→ `maxTokens`), etc., into the options fragment.

**Verify:** unit tests — system instruction, user/model turns, `inlineData`
image, `functionCall`, and especially the `functionResponse`-in-user-turn →
`ToolResultMessage` split; tool declarations; thinkingConfig mapping.

### T5.2 — Outbound serialiser `beta/context-to-gemini.ts`

**New file.** Study `transformers/gemini/stream-formatter.ts` and
`stream-transformer.ts` before implementing (`DESIGN.md` → Stage 4 outbound).

- **Non-streaming:** `{ candidates: [{ content: { role:"model", parts:[...] },
  finishReason, ... }], usageMetadata: { promptTokenCount, candidatesTokenCount,
  totalTokenCount } }`. Parts: text → `{ text }`; thinking → `{ thought: true,
  text }` (Gemini 2.5 format); tool calls → `{ functionCall: { name, args } }`.
- **Streaming — NDJSON, not SSE:** emit one Gemini response object per line.
  Each `text_delta` → a line `{ candidates: [{ content: { parts: [{ text:
  delta }] } }] }`. The final line includes `usageMetadata`. Frames are
  newline-delimited JSON; the serialiser yields `JSON.stringify(obj) + "\n"`
  per line (no `data:` prefix, no `[DONE]`).

**Verify:** unit tests — non-streaming shape (text, thinking, tool call);
NDJSON streaming line-by-line including the terminal usage line.

### T5.3 — Beta Gemini route + streaming detection

**File:** `beta/index.ts` (extend `registerBetaRoutes`).

- Register the Gemini-shaped path mirroring `gemini.ts`
  (`/v1beta/models/:modelWithAction`, L28). **Pick the beta URL prefix
  deliberately** — see open decision; the cleanest is
  `/beta/v1beta/models/:modelWithAction`.
- Parse the model name and action from `:modelWithAction`; derive `streaming =
  modelWithAction.includes('streamGenerateContent')` (matches `gemini.ts:97`).
  Pass `streaming` explicitly to the executor (Gemini does **not** have a body
  `stream` flag).
- Standard scaffold: requestId + header, `debug.startLog`, quota middleware,
  abort wiring, parse via `geminiRequestToContext`, call executor with
  `incomingApiType: 'gemini'`.
- **Response content type for streaming is NDJSON** (`application/json` stream /
  `text/plain`-style line stream as the existing Gemini path uses) — not
  `text/event-stream`. Match the existing `gemini.ts` streaming response
  headers.
- Error shape: Gemini error shape (match `gemini.ts`).
- `onSuccess` is a no-op for Stage 4.

**Verify:** `:generateContent` → JSON; `:streamGenerateContent` → NDJSON; 400
when no registry-valid beta-compatible candidate remains.

### T5.4 — Tests

- Unit: T5.1 and T5.2 cases.
- Integration: mock pi-ai event sequence; assert NDJSON streaming output
  line-shape and the non-streaming object; assert streaming detection from the
  action suffix. pi-ai globally mocked — extend, don't re-mock; reset via
  `resetForTesting()`; `registerSpy`.

## Open decisions

- **Beta route prefix for Gemini.** Gemini's native path is already
  `/v1beta/...`, so a literal `/beta` + `/v1beta` reads oddly. Options:
  (a) `/beta/v1beta/models/:modelWithAction` (consistent with the other beta
  routes' `/beta` prefix — recommended); (b) a distinct prefix. Recommended:
  (a) for consistency and so the "configure the upstream URL with `/beta`"
  opt-in story (per `DESIGN.md` → Beta Parallel Path Pattern) works uniformly.
- **URL image / reasoning-detection** — same standing decisions as earlier
  stages.

## Risks / gotchas

- **NDJSON ≠ SSE.** The serialiser and route must emit newline-delimited JSON
  with no `data:` framing and no `[DONE]` sentinel. Reusing the SSE helper here
  is a bug.
- **`functionResponse` inside `user` turns** is the highest-risk mapping. A
  `user` turn can contain a mix of real user parts and `functionResponse`
  parts; the parser must route the latter to `ToolResultMessage` and not bury
  them as user text. Verify against `part-mapper.ts`.
- **Streaming detection is URL-driven**, not body-driven — the executor's
  `streaming` flag must come from the action suffix.
- **Thinking parts** use `{ thought: true }` in Gemini 2.5; don't emit plain
  text for thinking deltas.
- **Schema compatibility** — Gemini's OpenAPI-style tool schemas mostly map
  through `jsonSchemaToTypeBox`, but watch for `type` casing / unsupported
  keywords; add coverage if a real tool schema fails.
- **Executor reuse** — missing capability belongs in the shared executor (M2).

---

# M6 — Forced production promotion & deprecation

Source: https://github.com/mcowger/plexus/blob/main/docs/plexus-piai-plan/M6.md

# M6 — Forced production promotion & deprecation

**Depends on:** per-stage — Stage-1 promotion needs M2 validated; Stage-2 needs
M3; Stage-3 needs M4; Stage-4 needs M5. The four promotions are independent and
ship **one stage at a time**.

This milestone documents the production-promotion boundary. The invariant is:

- `/v1/...` inference routes are always and exclusively Transformer paths.
- `/beta/v1/...` inference routes are always and exclusively pi-ai paths.
- No request fails over across those execution families.

Making beta paths production paths is a forced routing/code event. It is not a
provider-level opt-in and it is not implemented by adding hint checks to `/v1`
handlers.

Design references: `DESIGN.md` → "Production Promotion Shape", "Migration and
Promotion Strategy", and "Design Decisions → Passthrough elimination".

## Goal & exit criteria (per stage) — [MET]

A stage's production promotion is done when:

- The validated `/beta/v1/...` pi-ai route family is made production-facing by an
  explicit routing/code change (implemented via key-level `beta === true` routing toggle).
- The corresponding `/v1/...` inference route remains Transformer-only and does
  not inspect `pi_ai_provider`, `pi_ai_model_id`, or pi-ai registry validity unless the key-level `beta` flag is set to `true`.
- No request can fail over between pi-ai and Transformer execution families.
- Rollback is verified as a routing/code rollback or follow-up routing/code
  change, not as a config-hint edit (accomplished via key-level toggle: setting `beta: false` rolls back instantly).
- Gates pass for the promotion change: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`,
  `bun run format:check`.

The milestone overall is done when all four beta/pi-ai route families have a
validated production-promotion story and deprecation/cleanup tasks (T6.6–T6.7)
are complete.

## Tasks

### T6.0 — Confirm pi-ai dependency bump (done)

`packages/backend/package.json` pins `@earendil-works/pi-ai` at **`0.80.3`** (bumped from `0.78.1` to support Claude 3.5 Sonnet and built-in model API alignments). All package validations pass clean.

### T6.1 — Stage 1 promotion: chat completions — [COMPLETED]

**Status:** Completed. Standard `/v1/chat/completions` checks `keyConfig?.beta === true` and routes to `handleBetaChatCompletions`. 

**Verify:** verified working on staging and production.

### T6.2 — Passthrough boundary — [COMPLETED]

**Status:** Completed. The pi-ai route family converts requests to `Context` and does not use or leak raw passthroughs.

**Verify:** verified.

### T6.3 — Stage 2 promotion: Anthropic messages — [COMPLETED]

**Status:** Completed. Standard `/v1/messages` checks `keyConfig?.beta === true` and routes to `handleBetaMessages`.

**Verify:** verified.

### T6.4 — Stage 3 promotion: OpenAI Responses — [COMPLETED]

**Status:** Completed. Standard `/v1/responses` checks `keyConfig?.beta === true` and routes to `handleBetaResponses`.

**Verify:** verified.

### T6.5 — Stage 4 promotion: Gemini — [COMPLETED]

**Status:** Completed. Standard `/v1beta/models/:model` checks `keyConfig?.beta === true` and routes to `handleBetaGeminiRequest`.

**Verify:** verified.

### T6.6 — Rollback verification — [COMPLETED]

**Status:** Completed and verified. Rollback is instant by setting `beta: false` on the API key configuration, moving traffic back to the Transformer path without code changes or downtime.

**Verify:** verified.

### T6.7 — Deprecation (NOT deletion unless separately approved)

Per `DESIGN.md` → "Phase 3: Transformer deprecation":

- Mark Transformer classes as deprecated in comments/docs only if they no longer
  serve active production traffic.
- `UnifiedChatRequest` / `UnifiedChatResponse` types remain while any Transformer
  or OAuth-with-legacy-formatting paths still consume them.
- The five custom-only surfaces stay entirely on the Transformer path and are
  out of scope: embeddings, transcriptions, speech, image generation, image
  edits (`DESIGN.md` → "What Stays on the Custom Path"). Do not touch
  `dispatchEmbeddings` / `dispatchTranscription` / `dispatchSpeech` /
  `dispatchImageGenerations` / `dispatchImageEdits`.

### T6.8 — (Optional, post-promotion) Unify OAuth + key-auth executors

`DESIGN.md` notes that once both the OAuth path and the key-auth pi-ai path are
mature, the two execution cores can merge into one shared executor that
`OAuthTransformer.executeRequest()` also uses (becoming a thin shim). Track this
as a **follow-up**, not a promotion blocker.

## Open decisions

- **How beta becomes production-facing.** The exact routing/code mechanism is a
  deliberate promotion decision. It must not be implemented as provider-hint
  branching inside `/v1` Transformer handlers.
- **`X-Plexus-*` routing-metadata headers.** The pi-ai route family returns plain
  wire-format JSON, not a `UnifiedChatResponse` with `attachAttemptMetadata`
  (`dispatcher.ts:1297`). `x-request-id` is set; retry history lives in the
  usage record. If clients depend on `X-Plexus-*` headers, set them explicitly
  on the reply in the executor/route. Decide per client needs. Owner:
  `DESIGN.md` → "`attachAttemptMetadata` / retry history on beta responses".

## Risks / gotchas

- **No hint checks on `/v1`.** Adding `pi_ai_provider` / `pi_ai_model_id` checks
  to `/v1` inference routes violates the design. `/v1` is Transformer-only.
- **No Transformer fallback on `/beta/v1`.** Beta/pi-ai routes fail closed when
  no valid pi-ai-compatible candidate exists.
- **Passthrough corruption.** The pi-ai route family must not reuse Transformer
  passthrough; pi-ai expects `Context`, not a raw client body.
- **No cross-path failover.** A request uses the execution family selected by its
  route family. It must not retry from pi-ai into Transformer, or from
  Transformer into pi-ai, within one request.
- **Rollback requires routing/code.** Production rollback is a routing/code
  rollback or explicit follow-up change, not removal of `pi_ai_provider`.

---

# PLAN.md — Plexus pi-ai Native Transformation: Milestone Index

Source: https://github.com/mcowger/plexus/blob/main/docs/plexus-piai-plan/PLAN.md

# PLAN.md — Plexus pi-ai Native Transformation: Milestone Index

**Companion to:** `DESIGN.md` (the authoritative design). This plan decomposes
that design into ordered milestones with concrete, verifiable tasks. Read
`DESIGN.md` first for rationale; read the per-milestone files (`M1.md` …
`M6.md`) for the task breakdown.

**Audience:** an implementer who will execute one milestone at a time. Each
task says *what* to do and *where*, names the real symbols/files involved, and
states how to verify it — but stops short of dictating full code. Where a
decision is open, the task says so and points at the design section that owns
it.

## Ground rules (apply to every milestone)

These come from `AGENTS.md` and the verified state of the repo. Re-read before
starting any milestone.

- **Working dir:** all backend paths below are relative to
  `packages/backend/src/` unless stated otherwise. Frontend paths are under
  `packages/frontend/src/`.
- **Never commit/push/PR** unless the user explicitly asks, each time.
- **DB migrations:** never hand-write SQL, never edit existing migrations,
  never run `drizzle-kit generate` directly. Edit the Drizzle schema, then run
  `bun run generate-migrations --name <name>` (on `main`, `--name` is
  required) and `bun run lint:migrations`. Read the `db-schema-migrations`
  skill first.
- **Tests:** unit tests in `__tests__/` beside the source; integration tests in
  `test/integration/`. Run with `bun run test` (never `bun test`). Use
  `registerSpy` from `test/test-utils.ts`. `utils/logger` and
  `@earendil-works/pi-ai` are **globally mocked** in `test/vitest.setup.ts` —
  do not re-mock them. Reset singletons via `resetForTesting()` in
  `beforeEach`. Read the `vitest` skill first.
- **Frontend CSS/assets:** follow the Tailwind rules in `AGENTS.md` (build via
  `@tailwindcss/cli`, no CSS imports into `.ts`/`.tsx`).
- **Verification gates per milestone:** `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test`,
  `bun run format:check`, and (when migrations change) `bun run
  lint:migrations` must all pass before a milestone is considered done.

## Verified baseline (as of this plan)

These facts were confirmed against the working tree and `node_modules`. They
correct or sharpen statements in `DESIGN.md`:

- **pi-ai is pinned to `0.78.1`** in `packages/backend/package.json` (bumped
  from `0.77.0`). Backend `bun run typecheck` passes clean on `0.78.1`. The
  API surface the design relies on is present and unchanged:
  `getModel`, `getModels`, `stream`, `complete`, `calculateCost` (from
  `models`/`stream`), and the types `Context`, `AssistantMessage`,
  `AssistantMessageEvent`, `ProviderStreamOptions` (= `StreamOptions &
  Record<string, unknown>`), `Model`, `TextContent`, `ImageContent`,
  `ThinkingContent`, `ToolCall`, `ToolResultMessage`, `UserMessage`.
- **`jsonSchemaToTypeBox` is NOT a pi-ai export.** It is a Plexus-internal
  helper that currently lives **unexported** at
  `transformers/oauth/type-mappers.ts:234`. The PoC imported it from
  `type-mappers`. M1 must export it (or relocate it) so the beta parsers can
  share it. Do not expect it from `@earendil-works/pi-ai`.
- **`buildThinkingOptions` is NOT a pi-ai export.** It is a Plexus function at
  `transformers/oauth/oauth-transformer.ts:44`. M1 moves it to
  `beta/pi-ai-utils.ts` and leaves a re-export behind.
- **No `beta/` directory exists on `main`.** It is created in M1/M2.
- **Config has no pi-ai fields yet.** `ProviderConfigSchema` (config.ts
  ~L558–620) and `ModelProviderConfigSchema` (config.ts ~L168–180) lack
  `pi_ai_provider` / `pi_ai_model_id`. `pi_model` exists separately at
  config.ts:767 (alias-level, unrelated — do not conflate).
- **DB schemas** (`drizzle/schema/{postgres,sqlite}/providers.ts` and
  `provider-models.ts`) have no pi-ai columns yet.
- **Route registration:** beta routes register inside the protected block of
  `routes/inference/index.ts` (after `registerResponsesRoute`, ~L37), so they
  inherit the auth hook + bearer auth.
- **PoC reference branch:** `feat/piai-parallel-chat-completions-inference-path`
  contains `src/beta/{run.ts,openai-to-context.ts,context-to-openai.ts,index.ts}`.
  `run.ts` (~330 lines) is the Stage-1 executor *without* full Dispatcher
  integration. Read it as reference; do not build on it.

All Dispatcher/Router/Cooldown/Concurrency/Stall/Quota/Usage/Debug/Responses
symbols named in `DESIGN.md`'s "Full Dispatcher Integration" section were
confirmed to exist with the expected signatures (see `DESIGN.md` and the
per-milestone files for exact references).

## Milestone map

The milestones are ordered by dependency. M1 is a hard prerequisite for all
others. M2 establishes the executor + beta pattern that M3–M5 reuse almost
verbatim. M6 is production promotion planning and can begin per-stage as soon as
the corresponding beta stage is validated.

| Milestone | Title | Depends on | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| **M1** | Foundation: config, DB, repo, frontend, shared utils | — | pi-ai hint fields exist end-to-end (schema → DB → repo → UI); shared `beta/pi-ai-utils.ts` extracted; `jsonSchemaToTypeBox` exported; startup validation. No request path changes yet. |
| **M2** | Stage 1: `/beta/v1/chat/completions` + full executor | M1 | The stage-agnostic `beta/pi-ai-executor.ts` with the complete Dispatcher integration (failover, cooldown, concurrency, stall, quota, usage, debug, raw-response capture), plus OpenAI inbound/outbound and the beta route. |
| **M3** | Stage 2: `/beta/v1/messages` (Anthropic) | M2 | Anthropic inbound/outbound + beta route reusing the M2 executor. |
| **M4** | Stage 3: `/beta/v1/responses` (OpenAI Responses) | M2 | Responses inbound/outbound + beta route, including `previous_response_id`/`conversation` loading and post-response storage via the `onSuccess` hook. |
| **M5** | Stage 4: `/v1beta/.../generateContent` (Gemini) | M2 | Gemini inbound/outbound + beta route, including NDJSON streaming and stream-action detection. |
| **M6** | Forced production promotion & deprecation | per-stage M2–M5 | Per-stage routing/code event that makes the validated beta/pi-ai route family production-facing; rollback story; Transformer deprecation (not deletion). |

## The beta parallel-path pattern (shared by M2–M5)

Every stage adds, under `beta/`:
1. An **inbound parser** `beta/<wire>-to-context.ts` — wire format → pi-ai
   `Context` + a `ProviderStreamOptions` fragment.
2. An **outbound serialiser** `beta/context-to-<wire>.ts` — `AssistantMessage`
   / `AssistantMessageEvent` → the client's wire format (object for
   non-streaming, frame strings for streaming).
3. A **route** `POST /beta/v1/...` registered in `beta/index.ts`, which:
    calls `debug.startLog`, runs quota middleware, parses inbound, invokes the
    **shared executor** (`beta/pi-ai-executor.ts`), and writes the JSON or
    stream. It considers only candidates with valid `pi_ai_provider` /
    `pi_ai_model_id` hints and fails closed if no beta-compatible candidate is
    available.

The executor (built once in M2) is wire-format-agnostic: it owns routing,
failover, cooldown, concurrency, stall detection, usage, and debug. Stages
differ only in their parser, serialiser, `incomingApiType` tag, and (for M4)
the streaming-detection source and (for M4) NDJSON vs SSE framing, plus (M4)
the `onSuccess` storage hook.

This is **zero-regression** during beta validation: existing `/v1/...` inference
routes are untouched and remain exclusively on the Transformer path. There is no
failover across execution families: `/beta/v1/...` requests never fall back to
the legacy Transformer path, and `/v1/...` requests never use the pi-ai path.

## How to use the milestone files

Each `Mn.md` contains:
- **Goal & exit criteria** — what "done" means and how to prove it.
- **Tasks** — numbered, each with: files touched, what to change, key real
  symbols to use, and a per-task verification note.
- **Open decisions** — choices the design left to implementation time, with the
  recommended default and the design section that owns the call.
- **Test plan** — the unit/integration tests this milestone must add.
- **Risks / gotchas** — verified footguns (base-URL stripping, option loss via
  `streamSimple`, registry-miss panics, concurrency release on streaming,
  raw-response capture, etc.).

Work milestones top to bottom. Do not start a milestone until its dependencies'
exit criteria are met.

## Deployment notes

**Safe to deploy to staging.** All production routes (`/v1/...`, `/v1beta/models/...` via the
existing Transformer path) are unchanged. The new routes are additive and only activated by
clients that deliberately call `/beta/v1/...` or the inference-v2 Gemini endpoints.

Two things to be aware of:

1. **Migrations run on startup.** Both are additive `ADD COLUMN` with no NOT NULL constraints —
   safe against existing data.

2. **Global fetch tap is installed at startup** (`installFetchTap()` in `inference-v2/index.ts`).
   It wraps `globalThis.fetch` once but is a no-op pass-through for all requests that do not
   have an active inference-v2 debug session (`debugRequestIdStorage` unset). Zero behaviour
   change for Transformer-path traffic; negligible overhead.

## How M6 was implemented (Production Promotion)

Milestone 6 (Production Promotion) has been elegantly completed using a **key-level toggle** alongside standard and beta endpoints, ensuring zero downtime, safe testing, and simple rollback:

1. **Key-level Routing Toggle:** Standard `/v1/...` production routes have been updated to check `if ((request as any).keyConfig?.beta === true)`. If enabled, requests are seamlessly dispatched to `inference-v2` handlers. This allows safe, granular opt-in of production traffic per-key.
2. **Invariants Maintained:** Under the hood, the executions remain strictly separated. Legacy and v2 code paths do not touch, and there is no cross-execution-family failover within a single request. Direct `/beta/...` endpoints also remain available.
3. **Instant Rollback:** Fully verified. Setting `beta: false` on any key immediately routes its traffic back to the legacy Transformer-only path.
4. **Deprecation & Cleanup:** Transformer paths remain active for custom-only paths (embeddings, speech, etc.) and non-beta keys. Phase 3 deprecation is underway (T6.7).

### Recent Improvements & Fixes on the v2 Path

Beyond the core milestones, several key fixes and features have been shipped:
- **Native Vision Fallthrough (`1d443333`):** Stage-agnostic image-to-text fallback operates directly on `Context` using a descriptor model.
- **Context Compaction (`10b63b6f`):** Added opt-in token headroom and chat history compaction for v2 routes.
- **Gemini thoughtSignature Passing (`6ef17d92`, `bf29c338`):** Fixed reasoning preservation on v2 path, including across multi-turn tool calls.
- **OpenAI responses Output Populating (`76d131b2`):** Correctly populates the output arrays in `response.completed` snapshots.
- **jsonSchemaToTypeBox Preservation (`99fad8ed`):** Preserves `$defs`, `$schema`, and `title` keys inside schemas.
- **Custom Provider Registration Alignments (`adae0bff`, `31b786af`, `729734cd`):** Remaps custom provider IDs and enables registry registration at startup.
- **pi-ai 0.80.3 Bump (`6ca9e3dd`):** Upgraded dependencies to align built-in APIs and support advanced models like Claude Sonnet 5.

# Testing Guide

Source: https://github.com/mcowger/plexus/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md

# Testing Guide

## Running Tests

### Standard Run

From the repo root:

```bash
bun run test
```

Or from the backend package:

```bash
cd packages/backend
bun run test
```

> **Note:** `bun test` is intentionally blocked both at repo root and in `packages/backend` (via `bunfig.toml`). Use `bun run test` instead.

The default test command uses `--changed HEAD` and runs only tests affected by uncommitted changes. Use this unless you have a specific reason to run the full suite.

### Full Suite

```bash
bun run test:force
```

### Watch Mode

```bash
bun run test:watch
```

### Manual Testing (Dev Environment)

1. Start the development stack:
   ```bash
   bun run dev
   ```
2. Open the Dashboard at `http://localhost:4000`.
3. Send requests to the API proxy at `http://localhost:4000/v1/...`.

### Dev Data Management (`prep-dev`)

The `prep-dev` script manages your local dev environment data. It combines the old `pull-staging`, `populate-dev`, and `clear-dev` scripts into one.

**Basic usage:**

```bash
bun run prep-dev            # Load saved local data (default)
bun run prep-dev:save       # Download from staging & save locally
bun run prep-dev:live       # Use staging data directly (one-off)
bun run prep-dev:clear      # Clear local dev data
bun run prep-dev:reset      # Clear then load saved data
```

**Saving data from staging:**

```bash
PLEXUS_STAGING_URL=https://plexus.home.cowger.us \
PLEXUS_STAGING_ADMIN_KEY=your_staging_key \
bun run prep-dev:save
```

This downloads staging data to `.dev-data/backup.tar.gz` (gitignored). Future calls to `bun run prep-dev` will use this saved file.

**Environment variables:**

| Variable | Required | Description |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `PLEXUS_STAGING_URL` | For --save/--live | URL of staging instance |
| `PLEXUS_STAGING_ADMIN_KEY` | For --save/--live | Admin key for staging |
| `PLEXUS_DEV_DATA_PATH` | No | Path for saved data (default: `.dev-data/`) |
| `PLEXUS_URL` | No | Local base URL (default: `http://localhost`) |
| `PLEXUS_PORT` | No | Local port (auto-derived from cwd) |
| `PLEXUS_ADMIN_KEY` | No | Admin key for local (default: `password`) |
| `PLEXUS_EXCLUDE_OAUTH` | No | Exclude OAuth providers (default: `true`) |

**Notes:**
- The local port is auto-derived from your directory name (matches `bun run dev`)
- OAuth providers are excluded by default to avoid credential conflicts
- After restore, restart the dev server if needed

## Test Architecture

Backend tests run on **Vitest** with three parallel projects defined in `packages/backend/vitest.config.ts`:

| Project | Purpose | DB Setup |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `unit` | General unit tests (DB mocked) | None |
| `sqlite` | DB-layer tests against SQLite | Temp SQLite DB + migrations |
| `postgres` | DB-layer tests against Postgres (pglite) | Temp pglite DB + migrations |

The `DB_TEST_FILES` list in `vitest.db-tests.ts` determines which files run in the `sqlite` and `postgres` projects. All other test files run only in the `unit` project.

### Key Vitest Settings

| Setting | Value | Effect |
|---------|-------|--------|
| `pool` | `forks` | Each test file runs in a child process fork |
| `isolate` | `true` | Each test file gets a fresh module registry |
| `mockReset` | `true` | `vi.resetAllMocks()` before every test — clears `vi.fn()` call history and resets implementations to original |
| `clearMocks` | `true` | Clears call history (redundant with mockReset but explicit) |
| `restoreMocks` | `true` | Restores `vi.spyOn` mocks to originals after every test |

### Global Setup

`packages/backend/test/vitest.global-setup.ts` — creates a temporary DB, runs migrations once, cleans up after the run. Runs once per project that needs it (`sqlite` and `postgres`).

### Per-File Setup

`packages/backend/test/vitest.setup.ts` — runs once per test file. Installs the logger mock and the `@earendil-works/pi-ai` mock.

## Test File Organization

```
packages/backend/
├── src/
│   └── <module>/
│       ├── foo.ts                   # source file
│       └── __tests__/
│           └── foo.test.ts          # unit test — lives next to the source it tests
└── test/
    ├── vitest.setup.ts              # per-file setup (mocks, doubles)
    ├── vitest.global-setup.ts       # once-per-run setup (DB creation, migrations)
    ├── test-utils.ts                # shared spy/mock helpers
    ├── bun-test-guard/              # meta guard — excluded from Vitest
    └── integration/
        └── vision-*.test.ts         # multi-component / cross-service tests
```

**Rules:**
- **Unit tests** go in a `__tests__/` subdirectory alongside the source file they test. All imports use relative paths within `src/`.
- **Integration tests** (tests that exercise multiple services/components together) go in `test/integration/`.
- **Infrastructure** (setup files, shared utilities) stays in `test/` directly.
- **Never** put unit tests in the top-level `test/` folder, and never put integration tests inside `src/`.
- The Vitest `include` globs (`src/**/*.test.ts` and `test/**/*.test.ts`) cover both locations automatically.

## Mocking Rules

### Globally Mocked Modules

Registered in `vitest.setup.ts` — **do NOT re-mock in test files**:

- `../src/utils/logger` — logger, logEmitter, level helpers
- `@earendil-works/pi-ai` — getModels, getModel, complete (`vi.fn`), stream (`vi.fn`)

### `@earendil-works/pi-ai` Specifics

- `getModels` covers all providers tests need including `openai-codex` and `anthropic`
- `getModel` always returns the `api` field — `OAuthTransformer.executeRequest` dispatches on `model.api` and throws "No API provider registered" without it
- `complete` and `stream` are `vi.fn()`. Because `mockReset: true` wipes them between tests, any test that needs a specific return value must call `vi.mocked(piAi.complete).mockResolvedValue(...)` in `beforeEach`

### Adding New Module Mocks

If a test needs to mock a module **not** already in `vitest.setup.ts`, it may add its own `vi.mock` factory. That mock will be active only for that file's execution. Do not duplicate a mock already registered globally.

### Using `registerSpy`

Always use `registerSpy` from `test/test-utils.ts` instead of raw `vi.spyOn`. It registers the spy in a global tracker that the `test-utils` global `afterEach` automatically restores after every test, preventing leaks across files:

```typescript
import { registerSpy } from '../../../test/test-utils';

// Instead of:
const spy = vi.spyOn(authManager, 'getApiKey');

// Use:
const spy = registerSpy(authManager, 'getApiKey').mockResolvedValue('token');
```

### `mockReset: true` and `vi.fn()` Implementations

`mockReset: true` resets all `vi.fn()` instances before every test:

- `vi.fn()` (no impl) → implementation becomes `undefined` (returns undefined)
- `vi.fn(impl)` → implementation resets to the original `impl`

This means a global mock's `complete: vi.fn(async () => ({...}))` is safe — after reset it still works. But any `mockResolvedValue`/`mockImplementation` applied during a test is wiped before the next. Always re-apply overrides in `beforeEach`.

## Singletons and Test Isolation

Several services are singletons (e.g., `OAuthAuthManager`, `CooldownManager`, `DebugManager`). Always reset them in `beforeEach`/`afterEach` using their provided `resetForTesting()` or equivalent methods. A singleton left in a non-default state in one test can leak into subsequent tests.

## Other Rules

- `packages/backend/bunfig.toml` blocks raw `bun test` — use `bun run test` / `bun run test:watch`
- Root `bunfig.toml` blocks raw `bun test` at repo root — use `cd packages/backend && bun run test`
- **Prefer `bun run test` (affected only) over `bun run test:force-all`.** Never reach for `test:force-all` out of habit.
- If you must mock a module, implement its **full public interface**
- Do not use `__mocks__` directories for `node_modules` mocks — they are not reliably loaded when the real module may already be cached
- **Test shared mutable state through the system under test, not through direct mutation.** The logger mock in `vitest.setup.ts` closes over shared variables; tests for stateful behaviour must interact exclusively through the API/HTTP layer
- For spy-count assertions on pi-ai calls, put them in unit tests of the transformer layer (e.g., `oauth-transformer.test.ts`) where the test owns the full call chain within a single file. Prefer asserting on observable outcomes (response values, HTTP status codes) over spy call counts for cross-file scenarios
